title: Lesson 1: The Great Commission - Your Personal Ministry
description: On a mountain in Galilee, Jesus sent ordinary, unsure followers to make disciples of all nations. This lesson shows you that you are sent too, starting with the people already around you.

blocks.text: Welcome to Growing Out

The 200-level path has three connected courses. Growing Deep (201) was about loving God. Growing Up (202) was about loving the people God has placed beside you. Now in Growing Out (203), the branches begin to bear fruit, as that love reaches people who do not yet know Jesus. Growing Up ended at the Lord's table, with gifts Jesus first gave to friends who were about to fail Him. Growing Out begins on a mountain, where He sends those same friends out.

blocks.alt: Growing Together Discipleship Series: Starting in Discipleship, Growing Out with the Gospel, and Leading in Discipleship

blocks.title: On the Mountain
blocks.text:
After Jesus rose from the dead, He told His disciples to meet Him in Galilee. So eleven men climbed a mountain there, "to the mountain to which Jesus had directed them" (Matthew 28:16). Not long before, every one of them had run away when He was arrested. Peter had denied Him three times beside a charcoal fire.

Then they saw Him, alive. "And when they saw him they worshiped him, but some doubted" (Matthew 28:17). Even on that mountain, with the risen Lord standing in front of them, some of them were still unsure.

Jesus did not send the doubters home to get stronger first. He did not go looking for a better team. He came to them, and He gave these forgiven, unsure, ordinary men the job of reaching the world.

And Jesus came and said to them, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age."

These are Jesus' last words in Matthew's Gospel, and last words carry weight. He did not give a farewell speech. He gave a commission: an assignment, a direction to move. These words have shaped the church for two thousand years, and they are addressed to you.

Three things anchor this commission. All authority has been given to Jesus, so He does not send you out on your own strength. All nations are in view, so no person, culture, or neighborhood is outside the reach of His mission. I am with you always, so the same presence that met the disciples on that mountain goes with you. The commission is impossible without those three anchors. With them, it is simply a matter of going.

Notice who Jesus sent: people who had failed Him and people who still had doubts. You do not have to be fearless or finished to be sent. You only have to belong to the One who sends you. You are sent, starting with the people already around you.
1.1 - Which of the three anchors speaks most to your fears about being sent?
You Are Sent
Jesus said to them again, "Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you."

The logic of this verse is exact: how the Father sent the Son is the pattern for how the Son sends you. And how was the Son sent? Into ordinary human life: a neighborhood in Nazareth, a carpenter's shop, meals with tax collectors, conversations at wells and in fishing boats. Jesus did not carry out His mission mainly through events or platforms. He carried it out through presence, showing up, noticing people, building trust, and letting the gospel work through everyday relationships. You are not supporting someone else's mission from a safe distance. You are sent.

Here is a shift that changes everything: Christians should be the missionaries. We should be crossing boundaries and going to people, not expecting people who have never been to church to cross every boundary and come to us. Think about the buildings you drive past every day, like a Masonic lodge, another church, or a community center, that you never think about entering. That is how most of the world drives past churches. The door feels unfamiliar and the customs feel foreign. The Great Commission does not say, "Wait and hope they come." It says, Go.
1.2 - How does John 20:21 change your picture of what a missionary is?
Your Personal Ministry Map
Matthew 28 gives the command. Acts 1:8 gives the map. These were Jesus' last words before He returned to the Father.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.

Jesus did not send His disciples to the end of the earth first. He started them in Jerusalem, the city where they already were, and then sent them out in widening circles. The global reach is real, and you will come back to it later in this course. But it always starts where you are right now. Many believers never become missionaries out in the world because they have never become missionaries at home, among the people who know them best and see them most.

The oldest picture of disciple-making in the Bible is a home where faith is woven into ordinary days. God told His people to talk about His words "when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise" (Deuteronomy 6:7). Your Jerusalem starts at your front door. Walk through your map below.

One question sits underneath your map: Does everyone who knows me know about the gospel? Not, have I preached at everyone? But have the people in my regular life seen enough of my faith and heard enough of my story to know what I believe and why? If not, your map shows you where to start.
1.3 - Start your map here. Write two or three names for each circle: home, work and school, and your neighborhood.
You Are Not Alone

Jesus ended the Great Commission with the most comforting words He ever spoke: "And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age." In Acts 1:8 He promised power when the Holy Spirit came. You do not go out alone. The Holy Spirit, whom you came to know in Growing Deep, lives in you, guiding you, giving you words when you do not have them, and opening doors you could not open yourself. This is a dependent adventure. The question is not whether you have enough skill. The question is whether you will step into the conversation and see where the Spirit takes you.

In the next four lessons, you will learn the BLESS rhythms, a simple way to love the people on your map: Begin with prayer, Listen, Eat, Serve, and Story. For now, the assignment is simple. Look at your map, pick one name, and ask God what He wants you to do this week.
1.4 - Who is one person on your map that God is placing on your heart this week?
Lesson 1 Review

On a mountain in Galilee, Jesus sent friends who had failed Him, and some who still doubted, and He promised to go with them. His last words are addressed to you too. He sends you with all authority behind you, all nations before you, and His presence with you always. You are sent the way the Father sent the Son, into ordinary life, starting with the people already around you: at home, at work or school, and in your neighborhood. Your Personal Ministry Map shows you where to begin, and you never go alone.
In the next lesson, you will begin the BLESS rhythms where every one of them starts, with prayer for the names on your map.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
